phase: Phase 3: The track A review set and the scorer (by Thu 2026-11-19)
summary: All six Phase 3 test files pass at HEAD with the labeled counts (17, 15, 21, 13, 10, 16), and the scorer matches D10 to D13 on window, nearer plant, duplicates, the 30-finding cap, invalid reviews, provisional passes, and rank; the 3.3a end-to-end test and T7b prove the score file reaches guide.ts and a provisional pass keeps its rank. One blocker: adjudicate.ts keys findings by a per-route position, so two routes cannot each get their own verdict, and scores can change. Five nonblocking findings cover the queue match window, two missed-count defects, the D7 key schema check, and one stale strategy line.
blocking_findings: P3A1-1 [Blocker] review-a: adjudicate.ts gives a finding the id `<diff_id>#F<n>` from its position in one route's output (line 264), but queue merges every route into one file and apply stores one verdict per id (lines 342-343). Reproduced: two routes with different claims at index 1 both emit id `forge-01#F1`, the two judge files can hold only one value for that id, and one judge `false-claim` then counts as a false claim for both routes. D11 says one finding is the unit and each finding gets its own verdict. False-claim counts, real-defect counts, and provisional flags can move between routes, which changes scores and rank. Tests J1 to J4 never run apply and the scorer for a second route with different claims; J1 dedupes identical claims only. Rationale: the track A rank depends on X in max(0, 100 F / W - 2 X), and control diffs make an index collision certain.
nonblocking_findings: P3A1-2 [Major] review-a: adjudicate.ts matchesPlant uses WINDOW = 2 (lines 81 and 164), so a finding at exactly new_lines[0] - 3 or new_lines[1] + 3 is queued as unmatched. D10 and the tool's own doc comment (lines 24-26) define the window as plus or minus 3, and review-score.ts uses 3. Reproduced: a finding at line 7 against plant [10, 15] is queued, while the scorer counts it found. A boundary finding judged real-defect then writes real_defects into the key and the PM hand-off for a finding D10 says must never reach adjudication. No test pins the queue match boundary.

P3A1-3 [Major] review-a: review-score.ts lines 275-277 skip the class and severity missed loop for an invalid review, so the plants of that diff are not counted missed in by_class and by_severity. This contradicts review-score.ts lines 48-53, which say a plant of an invalid diff is missed, and the recorded decision that missed counts plants no counted finding pointed at. Reproduced: one invalid review gives top-level missed 48, sum(by_class.missed) 44, and by_class.C1 missed 5 of 6. Test R4 asserts invalid_reviews, found, and score only.

P3A1-4 [Nit] review-a: the top-level missed (review-score.ts line 433, setPlants.length - counts.found) uses a different definition than by_class and by_severity missed, which count plants that no finding pointed at. Reproduced with the nearer-plant fixture: one record reports top-level missed 47 and sum(by_class.missed) 46. The recorded decision text matches only the class-level fields. One definition or the other needs to change so the two levels agree.

P3A1-5 [Major] review-a: review-set.ts does not check the D7 key schema that FR-8 names. Reproduced: delete new_lines, delete file, or delete witness from one plant, or set severity to critical; each mutation gives exit 0 and writes the manifest. A plant without file or new_lines can never match, and a severity outside the D6 scale gets weight 0 in review-score.ts (WEIGHTS[severity] ?? 0). Acceptance 9 treats a lint pass as a valid set.

P3A1-6 [Nit] review-a: test-strategy.md section 7 says review-score.test.ts calls the scorer in process. The test spawns a subprocess CLI (review-score.test.ts line 224). The decision is recorded in red-p3-a6e34c5.log and is sound, but the strategy line is false.

P3A1-1 reproduction: node script copied fixtures/review to /tmp/opencode/p3a-repro, wrote route_a with claims at index 1 and 2 and route_b with a different claim at index 1, ran adjudicate.ts queue, and read queue.json. Output: ITEM forge-01#F1 line 60 claim A; ITEM forge-01#F1 line 70 claim B; ITEM forge-01#F2 line 80; duplicate ids {forge-01#F1:2}. apply with both judges false-claim on forge-01#F1 wrote one verdict, and the scorer counted false_claims 1 for route_a and false_claims 1 for route_b from that single slot.

P3A1-4 reproduction: a score run with the nearer-plant fixture returned top missed 47 and sum(by_class.missed) 46 in one record.
P3A1-5 reproduction: four lint mutations (delete new_lines, delete file, delete witness, severity critical) each returned exit 0 with the manifest written.

Decision accepted: review-score is a subprocess CLI. The deviation is recorded in red-p3-a6e34c5.log before implementation, FR-9 describes a command, and the tests assert exit codes, stdout, and the written file. Consequence: the stale strategy line of P3A1-6.

Decision judged partial: missed counts the plants that no counted finding pointed at, whatever the class. It holds for by_class and by_severity on valid reviews (the nearer-plant test gives C2 {found:0,missed:5} with 6 C2 plants and one pointed plant). It fails for invalid reviews (P3A1-3) and at top level (P3A1-4).

Decision accepted: the K4 19-character boundary is not covered. leak-check.ts line 52 sets MIN_SEEDED_LENGTH = 20 and line 132 tests length >= 20, so a 19-character line passes by construction. Plan line 3.5 and red-3.5.txt record the deferral: the plan forbids the fixture that would exercise it.

Decision accepted: routes[].passes holds the pass records. red-3.3a.txt shows guide.ts refused the count form with exit 2 and 'input-check: scores'. Test R6, the 3.3a end-to-end test (route named with 'track A: worst 3.8 (n=3)'), and T7b pass at HEAD.
